title: That Pear Tallow Balm I Keep By the Sink
body:
So I’m standing there, it’s like 10:15 PM, and I’ve just washed my face for the third time today because pollen is a nightmare. My skin feels like that weird, tight paper they wrap around lightbulbs. I’m staring at the little jar next to my toothpaste. The whipped tallow balm. Pear scent. Sounds weird, right? Beef fat for your face. I thought it was a joke. My friend was like “just try it” and sent me a link to this Etsy shop in France. I figured, my skin can’t get much weirder, so why not. That was maybe six weeks ago. Now the jar’s half empty and I’m looking at it like an old friend. My tallow balm routine is basically just me slapping this on whenever my skin yells at me, which is often.

It started because my hands were a disaster. Like, cracking by the knuckles, rough, gross. I was using that blue stuff in the tub from the drugstore. Didn’t do anything. So one night, after doing dishes, I just scooped a tiny bit of this tallow stuff. A pea-size. Maybe smaller. Rubbed it in. It felt… thick at first. Kind of waxy? But then it was just gone. No greasy film. My hands just felt like hands again. Not “baby soft” or whatever. Just normal. Not painful. That was the hook.

## How This Beef Tallow Thing Ended Up on My Face

Look, I was skeptical. Putting beef tallow, which is literally rendered beef fat, on my face sounded like a prank. Or something my great-grandmother would have done. But the jar said it was from grass-fed cows and whipped into this creamy… balm. The texture’s strange. Not lotion. Not oil. It’s solid in the jar but melts the second you touch it. Like cold butter, but softer.

I read the little card that came with it. Said it mimics human skin sebum. Our own oils. So it absorbs deep instead of sitting on top. That made a dumb kind of sense. My fancy moisturizer that cost way too much just sat there, shiny. This tallow balm? It sinks in. Disappears. My skin drinks it. I started using it at night, after I shower. Just a tiny dab for my whole face. The size of a lentil. Seriously, a little goes a long way. I warm it between my fingers first. Smells like pear. Not candy pear. Like a real, kinda green pear that’s not quite ripe. It’s light. Fresh. Not perfumey. Just… nice.

Sometimes my cat, Miso, jumps on the counter and sniffs the jar. He stares at it. I don’t know what he thinks it is.

## My Skin After a Few Weeks of This Stuff

Okay so the routine. It’s not fancy. Morning, if my skin feels tight (it’s spring, everything’s dry and windy), I’ll use a pinhead amount. Just on my cheeks and forehead. Then sunscreen over it. At night is the main event. After I wash my face—with that cheap Cerave cleanser, the green one—I pat it dry. Not bone dry. Damp. Then I take a bit more tallow balm, maybe the size of a small pea, and massage it in. Everywhere. Face, neck. Sometimes I get carried away and do my elbows. They’re always rough.

The change wasn’t overnight. But after a week or so, I stopped waking up with that tight, stretched feeling. My foundation, the little bit I wear, stopped clinging to dry patches. I had this one spot near my eyebrow that was always a little flaky. Gone. Just… not a thing anymore. I didn’t expect much but honestly it works. My skin just feels calm. Not “glowing” in a weird Instagram way. Just healthy. Like it’s not fighting me.

I told my mom about it. She has eczema on her hands. Real bad. I gave her my first jar when I ordered a second one. She texted me last week: “What was that cream? My knuckles don’t look red anymore.” High praise from her. She’s not easily impressed.

## Would I Buy This Pear Tallow Balm Again?

Yeah. I already did. I’m on my second jar. I keep one in the bathroom and one in my bag, this little tin version I got from the same Etsy shop. It’s called Maison something. I forget the full name. The label’s simple. Looks handmade. I like that.

It’s become a regular part of my daily skincare with tallow. It’s the step I actually look forward to. It’s not a chore. It’s this weird little moment of… I don’t know. It feels good. The smell is calming. The act of warming it up in my hands is calming. It’s like a reset button at the end of the day. For all the skepticism I had about using a beef tallow balm, it’s the simplest, most effective thing I’ve put on my skin in years. Better than the expensive stuff in the fancy glass bottles.

I was at the Walgreens on 5th, not the one by the highway, looking at the skincare aisle. All those bottles with twenty ingredients. I just left. Came home and used my tallow balm. It’s just one thing. One ingredient, basically. Sometimes that’s all you need.

## Quick Questions I Get Asked

**Is beef tallow good for your face?**
Weirdly, yes. From what I get, it’s similar to the oils our skin makes naturally. So it absorbs really well and doesn’t just clog stuff up. It’s like giving your skin back what it already knows how to use. My face seems to think it’s great.

**Does tallow balm clog pores?**
Not for me, and my skin can get congested. It absorbs deep. It’s not like putting Vaseline on. It melts in and disappears. If you use too much, yeah, maybe. But a tiny bit is all you need. Less is more.

**What does the pear tallow balm smell like?**
It’s subtle. Like a fresh, green pear. Not super sweet. Not like candy. Just a clean, fruity smell that fades pretty quick. It’s nice. Not overpowering at all.

Anyway. If your skin is being difficult, or dry, or just fussy, figuring out how to use tallow balm might be worth a shot. I was skeptical. Now I’m just… not. It just works. I don’t know what else to say. My skin’s happy, I’m happy. That’s all I wanted.
